metadata.summary: A dataset of 10,015 dermatoscopic images of pigmented skin lesions collected from two sources: a hospital-centered archive of the Department of Dermatology at the Medical University of Vienna, and a smaller public repository of the ISIC Archive. Annotated with 7 diagnostic categories for training and benchmarking machine learning models for automated skin lesion classification.
metadata.custodian: Medical University of Vienna; ISIC Archive
metadata.purpose: Training and benchmarking machine learning models for automated skin lesion classification.

papers.title: The HAM10000 dataset, a large collection of multi-source dermatoscopic images of common pigmented skin lesions

ethics.privacy_measures: Images were de-identified prior to release; no patient identifiers retained.
ethics.legal_compliance: Compliant with Austrian data protection law and ISIC Archive policies.

extraction.notes: 基线卡仅来自 dataset_catalog.xlsx 真实元数据；其余字段需论文/README 或人工补充。
pending_verification: 以下 LLM 字段因不符合 schema 约束已自动丢弃并回退基线值，待人工核实：data_collection_setting, medical_fields[list-items]

known_limitations: Predominantly Austrian (Caucasian) population limits generalizability to darker skin tones.
Convenience sampling from clinical archives introduces selection bias toward more common or clinically suspicious lesions.
Lack of standardized acquisition protocol across sources (hospital vs. ISIC).
Label noise due to reliance on clinical vs. histopathological confirmation.
bias_and_limitations.modifications: No synthetic data; minor preprocessing (cropping, resizing) applied for uniformity.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: Overwhelmingly Caucasian population; limited representation of Fitzpatrick skin types IV–VI.
bias_and_limitations.long_tail_classes: Yes — some diagnostic categories (e.g., vascular lesions) are underrepresented.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Limited generalizability to non-Caucasian populations and non-dermatology-clinic settings.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: No explicit reporting of missing clinical or demographic metadata.

tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Detection and segmentation are not supported by current annotation format (single-label image-level only).

data_origin.selection_rationale: To meet the need for a publicly available standard benchmark for skin lesion classification.
data_origin.sampling_strategy: Convenience sampling from two sources: hospital archive (majority) and public ISIC repository (minority).
data_origin.aggregation_multisource: Aggregated from two sources: hospital-centered archive (Medical University of Vienna) and ISIC public repository; no description of harmonization or recoding.

population.target_population: Patients with pigmented skin lesions undergoing dermatologic evaluation.
population.inclusion_criteria: Pigmented skin lesions imaged dermoscopically and diagnosed by dermatologists.
population.missing_groups: No explicit demographic subgroup statistics stated in the abstract; underrepresentation of non-Caucasian skin types is a known concern in dermoscopy datasets but not quantified here.

annotation.annotation_method: Diagnoses assigned by board-certified dermatologists; labels derived from clinical diagnosis and histopathology where available.
annotation.labeling_provenance: Clinical diagnosis and histopathology where available.
annotation.label_noise_description: Some labels may reflect clinical (not histopathological) diagnosis; inter-observer variability acknowledged in source paper.
